1.why: Body text uses a clean sans/mono-style face with visibly wide letter spacing and roomy line height across all screens, though the typeface is not explicitly a dyslexia-specific font.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used anywhere; all copy appears as one- or two-line sentences with generous whitespace.

3.why: Content sits in a single narrow centred column with large tap-target buttons and stacked fields, which reads well at phone width, though the captures are desktop-width with wide empty margins.

4.why: Instructions such as 'Enter the six-digit code.' and 'Each code works once if you cannot use your authenticator.' are short and in plain language.

5.why: Every input shows an example placeholder: 'Example: 123456' for OTP codes, 'Example: ABCD-EFGH-JKLM' for recovery codes, and 'marcus@example.com' for email.

6.why: The longest text on any screen is two short lines; no dense paragraph must be read to advance.

7.why: Step 6 provides 'Copy setup secret' for the long base32 string and steps 8–9 provide 'Copy all codes' for the recovery code list.

8.why: Step 5 shows a scannable QR setup pattern via 'Show QR setup pattern', explicitly offered as an alternative to the manual secret.

9.why: Fields look like standard inputs with helpful placeholders, but nothing in the screenshots demonstrates autocomplete/one-time-code attributes or password-manager integration, so this cannot be confirmed.

10.why: A four-segment progress bar, a clear H1 per screen and a single filled blue primary button make position and next action visible, though the progress segments are unlabelled.

11.why: Each screen has exactly one filled primary button, though steps 4–6 and 8–9 also present several secondary buttons (show QR, show secret, copy, use a recovery code) at once.

12.why: Green status banners plainly report outcome and next step, e.g. 'Identity checked. Next, set up your authenticator.' and 'Authenticator confirmed. Now save your recovery codes.'

13.why: 'Request another code', 'Show/Hide QR setup pattern', 'Show/Hide setup secret', 'Show/Hide recovery codes', 'Create recovery codes' and 'Test a recovery code' all allow free retry and reveal/hide without penalty.

14.why: The only error seen, 'Your page check expired. Refresh the page and try again.', names the problem and the fix without blaming, but 'page check' is vague jargon and no field-level validation errors are demonstrated.

15.why: Steps 14–15 show a 'page check expired' error, evidence that a hidden session/token timeout does elapse while the user reads, so the claim of no time limit does not hold.
